name: Technical University of Munich
summary: TUM is a public technical university in Bavaria, founded in 1868 as the Royal Bavarian Polytechnic School. It enrolled 51,954 students in winter semester 2025/26, about 45% of them international. Non-EU bachelor's students pay tuition of EUR 2,000 or 3,000 per semester depending on the program.

totalStudents.notes: Figure quoted in a search-result summary of the TUM 'TUM in figures' page; tum.de could not be fetched directly.

internationalShare.notes: Share of total enrolment, as quoted in a search-result summary of the TUM 'TUM in figures' page.

applicationPlatform.value: TUM online application portal; applicants with a non-German school certificate must first obtain a Preliminary Documentation (VPD) from uni-assist (Indian applicants also need an APS certificate)
applicationPlatform.notes: Via search-result summaries of tum.de pages (tum.de blocked to fetch).

testing.notes: No general SAT/ACT requirement found on TUM pages; admission is by program-level aptitude assessment.

internationalTuition.notes: TUM states bachelor's tuition for non-EU students is EUR 2,000 or 3,000 per semester depending on the program (x2 semesters). Informatics EUR 3,000/semester; Management and Technology (Munich) EUR 2,000/semester. A semester fee (EUR 97 in SS 2026 in Munich/Garching) is charged on top. Waivers exist for some students.

domesticTuition.notes: TUM tuition applies only to students from non-EU countries; EU/EEA students pay only the semester fee (EUR 97 per semester in SS 2026, Munich/Garching/Weihenstephan).

scholarships.name: TUM Scholarship for International Students
scholarships.eligibility: Students not eligible for BAföG because of nationality; enrolled at TUM from the 3rd bachelor's semester (2nd master's semester); good academic record and proven financial need.
scholarships.coverage: One-time financial aid of EUR 500 to EUR 1,800 per semester; reapply each semester, maximum funding period 36 months

scholarships.name: Deutschlandstipendium at TUM
scholarships.eligibility: Admitted or enrolled TUM students including international students new to TUM; considers achievement, commitment, responsibility and personal circumstances. Recipients must be resident in Germany with a German bank account.
scholarships.coverage: EUR 300 per month, half federal and half private sponsor

scholarships.name: Tuition fee waivers for international students
scholarships.eligibility: Waiver rules for non-EU tuition are set out on TUM's tuition page; the student-union semester fee is not waived. Specific criteria not verified here.
scholarships.coverage: Waiver of non-EU tuition fees where granted

opportunities.name: UnternehmerTUM and TUM Venture Labs
opportunities.description: TUM students can use the entrepreneurship offers of TUM, UnternehmerTUM and the TUM Venture Labs free of charge; TUM-linked teams launched a record 103 start-ups in 2024.

opportunities.name: TUMexchange and scholarships for stays abroad
opportunities.description: TUM Global runs exchange programs and publishes scholarship and funding options for stays abroad.

programs.name: Informatics (B.Sc.)
programs.school: TUM School of Computation, Information and Technology
programs.summary: Six-semester, 180 ECTS bachelor's program taught in German, located at Garching, starting in the winter semester. Admission is by aptitude assessment (points-based first stage, then a written test for some applicants).

requirements.notes: TUM classifies the IB Diploma as an international higher education entrance qualification; whether it gives general or subject-restricted access is decided by the uni-assist VPD. Program-specific IB subject/grade requirements not found. The program is German-taught: German proficiency certificate is required in addition.

A-levels are listed by TUM among qualifications that are checked by uni-assist. TUM states that if a foreign certificate is not comparable to the German Abitur, admission is possible only after the Studienkolleg and Feststellungsprüfung. Program-specific A-level subjects/grades not found.

NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN. DAAD India states that a Class XII certificate from any Indian board does not give direct admission to a German university (exception: valid JEE Advanced result for subject-specific access); otherwise Studienkolleg (about 1 year) plus the Feststellungsprüfung is needed. TUM additionally requires Indian applicants to submit school certificate, university entrance exam results, transcript and an APS certificate through uni-assist. Figures taken from search-result summaries; confirm with uni-assist VPD.
Same as CBSE: NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN (Class XII from any Indian board); Studienkolleg + Feststellungsprüfung, or JEE Advanced for subject-specific access; APS certificate required by TUM.
Not verified. All non-German certificates require a uni-assist VPD; if not comparable to the Abitur, the Studienkolleg route applies.

tests.test: TUM Informatics aptitude assessment (written test, 90 minutes, about 20-30 questions in English)
tests.notes: Two-stage procedure: stage 1 awards points from school grades, subject grades and relevant experience; applicants are admitted, rejected or invited to the written test depending on points.

tests.test: German proficiency (TestDaF level 4 in all sections, DSH-2, telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule, Goethe C2, DSD II B2, Austrian Sprachdiplom C2)
tests.notes: Program is taught in German. Proof must be submitted before the application deadline. Winter-semester application period is 15 May to 15 July (generic; exact 2027 dates not verified).

fees.notes: EUR 3,000 per semester for non-EU students, per the program page.

programs.name: Management and Technology (B.Sc., Munich campus)
programs.summary: Taught in English (100% English or bilingual track offered). Admission is by a two-stage aptitude assessment including a group interview.

subjects.subject: Mathematics
subjects.notes: Grades in German or English, Mathematics and an advanced natural science subject (including Informatics) from the last two years of school enter the stage-1 score.

requirements.notes: IB is named as an accepted secondary certificate; uni-assist evaluation is mandatory for international certificates. Stage 1 (Abitur example): 88+ points direct admission, 67-87 interview, 66 or less rejection; stage 2 interview needs 70+ points. Exact conversion for IB scores not found.
A-levels are evaluated by uni-assist; if not comparable to the Abitur, Studienkolleg + Feststellungsprüfung is required. Program-specific A-level subject/grade requirements not found.

NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN. Class XII from an Indian board does not give direct admission to German universities per DAAD India (exception: JEE Advanced for subject-specific access); Studienkolleg + Feststellungsprüfung otherwise. TUM requires an APS certificate for Indian applicants.
NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN, as for CBSE.

tests.test: TUM School of Management aptitude assessment (stage 1 grade-based score; stage 2 group interview of about 50 minutes)
tests.notes: If half-year grades in English for the last two years of school cannot be shown, applicants are invited to an interview conducted in English.

fees.notes: EUR 2,000 per semester for non-EU students (as quoted in search summary of the mgt.tum.de page). No English language certificate is required for this program; proficiency is assessed in the selection procedure. Application window for winter semester: until 15 July (generic).
